summary: Feed s112_double to IDS is degraded: 9.5% of frames exceed the IDS 1518B MTU and are dropped by the NIC, and 70.7% of traffic is still GRE-encapsulated, hiding inner payload from inspection. Both faults cause significant detection blind spots.

findings.root_cause: Upstream network/broker delivering jumbo frames up to 8096B to a 1Gbps IDS port limited to 1518B without MTU normalization. 240 of 2529 frames (9.5%) exceed the tool's max_frame_bytes, indicating jumbo-enabled segments or broker egress not enforcing MTU.
findings.impact_on_tool: IDS NIC silently drops 9.5% of frames before inspection. Because this IDS needs full payload for signature matching, trimming/slicing is not viable and those flows go completely uninspected, allowing evasion.

recommended_fix.why: Tool needs full payload so slicing would break detection. Fix MTU end-to-end or configure packet broker to enforce 1518B egress MTU (fragment, filter or normalize jumbos) so frames are deliverable to the IDS NIC instead of being dropped.

findings.root_cause: Packet broker forwarding GRE-encapsulated traffic directly to IDS without decapsulation. 1788 of 2529 frames (70.7%) are GRE-wrapped, indicating missing strip-tunnel policy on the broker egress to this IDS.
findings.impact_on_tool: IDS sees only outer GRE/IP headers, not inner IP/TCP and application payload. Protocol parsing, signature matching and IOC detection fail on 70.7% of traffic, drastically reducing detection coverage.

recommended_fix.why: Stripping GRE at the packet broker exposes inner packets for full IDS inspection while preserving encapsulation for other tools if needed. This restores visibility without requiring IDS to decode tunnels.
